answer: Paid demand is the gate: a seat is minted only after its operator carves a unique jade and sells it to a buyer funded from outside the operator's own circle. A prism audit refracts each payment into funding sources, so wash trades from one treasury collapse into a single line and are rejected; sales must clear a nadir price, making fake demand cost real money rather than recycled credits. A fleet of k clones needs k distinct jades and k unrelated buyers; genuine collectors are few, so each extra sale clears at a rising premium. One carving backs one seat, so pooled inventory mints nothing.
